headline: Supermarket freezers hacked again across Europe, Berlin's AI-nation plan, and a fuel price cap with a high trigger

stories.title: Hackers turn up supermarket freezers in Belgium, Sweden and Luxembourg, weeks after the French attack
facts: Overnight into Monday, fridge and freezer settings were changed remotely in dozens of stores: about 40 Delhaize and 15 Carrefour shops in Belgium, around five Spar stores, plus Delhaize in Luxembourg.
In Sweden several ICA stores and six or seven Coop stores were hit; one ICA store in Sjöbo says its freezers were set to 50 °C. The BBC also reports 13 SuperValu shops affected in Ireland.
Butcher chain De Laet & Van Haver says alarms went off at 3 a.m. after outside changes switched its evaporators into defrost mode.
Euronews cites Belgian reports of about €100,000 of food thrown away. Delhaize calls it an "IT incident", and ICA says the stores hit run outside its central network.
It mirrors the mid-October attack on hundreds of French Intermarché and Coopérative U stores, which hit Danfoss refrigeration; a link isn't confirmed and nobody has claimed it.
Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity says it is following the incident closely.
stories.whyItMatters: A second cross-border wave in three weeks suggests someone has a repeatable way into internet-connected store refrigeration, and food retail is now a proven target.

image.alt: An employee cleans freezers that are out of power at an ICA suparmarket on Odengatan in Stockholm, on November 2, 2026 after a number of ICA and Coop stores have suffered problems with their refrigerators and freezers overnight.

stories.title: Digital summit: Berlin wants Germany to be an "AI nation" by 2030
facts: Digital minister Karsten Wildberger opened the two-day Digital-Gipfel in Berlin: "We are still too slow."

The AI task force's final report sets 2030 targets: AI in at least 80% of large firms and 55% of SMEs, three times as many AI startups, over 10% of economic output AI-based, and AI in core work at 90% of federal agencies.
It lists 18 measures, including closer work with France and Canada, and says the window to catch up closes within the next 12 to 18 months.
Germany's planned AI safety institute is to cooperate with Canada.
The full report is due out around 16:00 Berlin today, and Chancellor Merz speaks at the summit this afternoon.
stories.whyItMatters: These are the first concrete numbers Berlin can be held to on AI, and economists say Germany is still poorly prepared.

stories.title: Reiche's fuel price cap draft only kicks in after three weeks of outsized price jumps
facts: The economy ministry's draft law would take effect on Jan 1, 2027, but the legal basis lasts only three months.

A cap isn't automatic: the government may set one only if German petrol or diesel prices rise more than 5 percentage points above the EU average in each of three straight weeks (pre-tax, per the EU's Weekly Oil Bulletin).
No price in cents is set yet; that comes later by ordinance. States may set their own regional caps, up or down, and the cap can be suspended if supply is at risk.
Breaches could cost up to €5m in fines.
The draft has only just entered early coordination inside the government.
stories.whyItMatters: The coalition promised the cap as a replacement for the fuel tax rebate, but as drafted it only triggers in an extreme price gap.

stories.title: Reporters Without Borders puts Trump on its press freedom predators list for the first time
facts: RSF's 2026 list names 33 "predators"; new entries include Donald Trump and Egypt's Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.
RSF says Trump uses the power of his office against media whose coverage he dislikes; the US ranks 64th of 180 in its index.
Also listed: FCC chair Brendan Carr, Alphabet and Meta (for draining ad revenue), Elon Musk, Vladimir Putin and China's Communist Party.
RSF Germany's Christian Mihr calls a US president next to Xi and Putin "a turning point", while noting Orbán and Vučić lost power.
The list marks today's International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a symbolic but sharp signal from the main press-freedom watchdog, landing on the eve of the US midterms.

stories.title: WIRED finds 400 harmless-looking AI apps hiding a sexual deepfake generator
facts: The network of over 400 apps and domains poses as pet-portrait, language or workout tools, then loads a hidden explicit-deepfake interface for some users, for example after clicking a Meta ad.
Researchers tie it to Chinese-language developers and a Hong Kong entity, KeLing Technology Limited, which didn't respond.
In September 27 of the apps were live on Google Play with over 350,000 downloads; one, DiffAI, passed 100,000.
Apple pulled 19 apps after WIRED asked and calls it a bait-and-switch after review; Google had removed most before being contacted.
Meta says it acted against 11,600 ad accounts and blocked 209 apps from advertising; similar ads kept appearing as WIRED finished the story.
stories.whyItMatters: App store review and ad moderation are being beaten by server-side switching, and the victims are people whose photos get uploaded.

facts.text: At the Manama Dialogue, Gulf diplomats fear a new US-Israeli strike on Iran soon after the US elections; a US carrier group is heading there and Iran threatens to cut the Gulf's internet cables.
Uganda has started pulling its troops out of the AU mission in Somalia after nearly 20 years; the phased exit is due to finish in August 2027.
Elon Musk says Grok Bot's running costs were "unsustainably high" relative to revenue, as users run into weekly limits.
Detroit techno pioneer Juan Atkins (Cybotron, Model 500) has died in Mexico City.
Tesla's Cybercab starts a European tour on Nov 5.

facts.text: Beyond OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic now back the shared robots.txt AI-training opt-out (User-Agent: __usage_ai-training); Microsoft honours it from Feb 1, 2027 and Google in early 2027.
Svelte fixed reactive context leaking past nested awaits in production builds.
SvelteKit's enhanced-img now computes a missing image dimension at runtime, and inline assets are read by UTF-8 byte length.
Tailwind CSS now parses a custom property at the end of input without a trailing semicolon.
